_comment: Fragment 9 — Step 1, G33b resolved. Merged 2026-08-20. Records D-52 and the four SPECS documents.

nodes.label: D-52 — G33b Resolved: 18 Candidates, 4 Documents
nodes.description: The D-30 redundancy test applied to all 18 SPECS candidates across the four Fn_Specs. Four outcomes: 7 absorbed into the S1 window, 9 requiring SPECS across 4 documents, 1 infrastructure-owned, 1 blocked by Q2. Two of the 18 are the same component named in two specs, so the 18 are 17 distinct. Only SPECS-TRANSITION-ENFORCEMENT is needed before S1.
nodes.rationale: The D-30 rule working as designed. Writing four SPECS documents mirroring the four Fn_Specs would have produced three documents nothing can act on and seven sections restating S1 window decisions. Mirroring the input structure is the redundancy failure in its most expensive form.

nodes.label: SPECS-TRANSITION-ENFORCEMENT — The Only Pre-S1 Document
nodes.description: The sequence-enforcement trigger: trigger timing, allowed-transitions table shape, and lock behaviour. The single SPECS document S1 requires. The other three — SPECS-BOARD-QUERY (S3), SPECS-PUBLICATION (S4, five components), SPECS-EXCEPTIONS (S5) — are sprint-aligned and not yet reachable.
nodes.rationale: FN-GATES-01-05 §9 claimed all five of its candidates absorb into the S1 window; verified, four do. This is the fifth. Accepting the claim as written would have concluded no SPECS was needed and left the gate sequence — the core invariant of the product — unspecified going into S1.

nodes.label: Mirroring the Input Structure Is the Redundancy Failure
nodes.description: The default failure mode D-30 exists to prevent: producing one output document per input document. Four Fn_Specs do not imply four SPECS. The correct decomposition here is by sprint and mechanism, which yields four documents covering nine components, only one of which is due before S1.
nodes.rationale: Structurally related to summary_outlived_source: both are cases where a derived artifact takes its shape from its source rather than from what it must determine. One restates counts, the other restates structure; both produce content that cannot be acted on.
